## Calculator

Make sure you know the rules.

```{r calculator}
7+3*9
32/4*4
```

Why doesn't Dushoff like the second one?

```{r parens}
print((32/4)*4)
```

## Assigning values to variables

```{r assign}
x <- 23
print(x)
```

What will happen here?

```{r no-assign}
x + 17
print(x)
```

What happened here?

```{r assign-y}
y <- x + 17
y
```

Question from card:

```{r card}
print(x+17)
```

NA is included generally because R likes to be over-inclusive.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Values in R

We need to understand: numeric, character and logical.

`str` tells us about the structure of a variable.

```{r numeric}
num <- 3
str(num)
```

Quotes make something into a character value instead of an R name.

```{r character}
char <- "Hello, class?"
str(char)
```

```{r logical}
logic <- TRUE ## No quotes
str(logic)
```

R's fundamental object is a *vector*. `c()` (concatenate) puts elements together into a vector.

```{r vectors}
words <- c("Mary", "had", "a", "little", "lamb")
str(words)

v <- 1:5  ## 'm:n' creates a sequence from m to n
str(v)
```

### Vector math

```{r vector-math}
v <- 1:5
w <- c(0, 1, 1, 2, 4)
v+w
print(w)
print(2*w)

mean(c(2, 5, 11))

x <- 1:10
m_x <- mean(x)
print(m_x)
```
